title: Frontend: Toggle button with custom hook
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Toggle button with custom hook. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Implement useToggle(initial) with toggle, on and off actions. App displays [data-testid="state"] on/off, starts off, and has Toggle, On, Off buttons. Functional toggle updates must compose.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Return the current boolean and stable operations for toggle, set true, and set false.
alternativeApproaches: Allow a controlled parent mode and define who owns state rather than mixing two authorities.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Default false; explicit true; two queued toggles.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
